title: Normative (law, code-contracts, decision/rules)

grammar.note: No grammar module yet. Normative rules are typed constraints; this family is design-only until the discrete/Z3 core of operations ships.

why_verify: Normative domains (law, code preconditions, regulated decisions) are the purest demand for 'agent may do only what well-defined rules permit.' An agent quoting a statute clause, applying a regulation, or proposing a code command must be checked against hardcoded rule text — and must be *disallowed silently* when a precondition fails, with a trace of exactly which rule and why.
how_handled_now: Contract attorneys + retrieval/grounding checks in legal AI; linters + sandboxes for code; compliance officers for regulated decisions. All either shallow (is the clause present in context?) or outside the agent loop (linting doesn't gate the agent's proposed step against the full rule set).
needs_before_ship: Z3 backend (same gate as operations family).
Rule compilation from structured, version-controllable rule text -> typed constraints.
conflicts() for 'which clause did this step violate'.
Code-specific: command/argument schema validation as preconditions (the tool-call contract).

logic.note: Left empty deliberately — no grammar exists; a filled-in list here would be fabrication. See scenarios for committed design contracts.

out_of_scope: declaring what the law *should* be (normative creation, not verification)

scenarios.plain: Agent, drafting a clause, asserts 'this contract provision permits data transfer to a third party without consent.' Prove against the hardcoded statute grammar (GDPR Article 6 legal basis required for transfer), or return the violated rule with evidence chain.
scenarios.note: Verification = legal rule compiled to typed precondition over a transfer fact; absence of a consent/legal-basis fact -> precond violated -> conflicts() names Article 6. This is verify-with-explanation, not grounding-match.

scenarios.plain: Agent proposes the command `sudo rm -rf ~/*`. Preconditions: (1) command must run in a sandbox, (2) human confirmation must be granted. Both are givens the agent cannot override; the execution transformation is legal only if both preconditions derive from state. Example enforces 'mountain ascent' — the agent may only step where rules allow.
scenarios.note: This is the frontier() operation's flagship scenario: legal-step membership from current state + hardcoded preconditions. None of it requires the agent to state or judge the rule. This scenario demonstrates the difference from both a generic guardrail (which reprompts) and a muddled composite: here the gate is a typed, traceable precondition on the command schema and state.

decisions.title: Normative family is design-only until discrete core ships
decisions.decision: law/code scaffolds happen after the Z3 operations core lands; no grammar is stubbed in code.
decisions.rationale: Normative rules and logistics rules share the same discrete-constraint engine. Building normative first would duplicate the Z3 work before it exists.

decisions.title: The `sudo rm -rf` example is the frontier() contract
decisions.decision: Sandbox + human-confirmation are hardcoded preconditions on execution; correctness of the example relies on the engine refusing the step when either precondition is absent, with a trace of which one.
decisions.rationale: Fixes the canonical demonstration of action-space gating: legal-step membership derived, never argued by the agent.

known_gaps: No rule-text compilation layer (statute/regulation -> typed constraints).
No command-schema validator fronting the code-contract case.
identity/sameAs policy unresolved (ARCHITECTURE.md section 9 q3) — matters when legal entities must be correctly merged.

out_of_scope.claim: LLM-judge deciding case outcomes or best argument
out_of_scope.why: judgment, not proof; statistical pipeline is not v1.
creation vs verification; out of scope.
